title: Lampu Cumi
subject: a squid-fishing crew stringing green lamps on their boat and racing the other boats out of Indramayu harbour at dusk
caption: Indonesian surf rock in the 1960s instrumental-band tradition, played by a modern West Java coast band. A clean lead electric guitar drenched in a spring-reverb tank playing rapid double-picked tremolo melodies with whammy-bar dips and reverb drips; a second guitar strumming reverb-soaked rhythm chords; a round electric bass driving the root notes; drums playing a pounding floor-tom surf beat with tom rumbles and the snare on two and four. Live and tight but wet with spring reverb, the lead guitar forward, the vocal rough and close. Rough, gritty male lead voice singing clear, plain melodies, with the boat crew shouting only the one-word answers. 168 BPM, E minor. Proud, salty and rowdy, a crew heading out to sea at dusk. No pop-punk chorus, no swing rhythm, no distorted metal guitar, no synths, no autotune.
lyrics:
[Intro - short spring-reverb tremolo pickup over floor toms, four bars]

[Verse 1]
Jam lima sore di muara Indramayu
Tiga puluh lampu kami ikat di tiang
Solar penuh, es balok dua ton
Mesin batuk dua kali, terus jalan

[Chorus - the crew shouts the answers]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Hijau di tengah laut gelap
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Cumi naik ke lampu kami

[Verse 2]
Kapal Haji Darman nyalip dari kiri
Juragan teriak, "Gas! Jangan kalah!"
Ombak setinggi pintu, kopi tumpah di dek
Kami yang duluan sampai di karang

[Instrumental Break - tremolo lead guitar with whammy dips]

[Chorus - the crew shouts the answers]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Hijau sampai kelihatan dari darat
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)
Cumi naik ke lampu kami

[Bridge - bass and floor toms alone, then the guitars crash back in]
Tiga minggu lagi kami pulang
Bawa cumi kering seratus karung
Kalau malam kamu lihat laut, Nak
Lampu hijau paling ujung itu Bapak

[Outro - one last tremolo run and a spring-reverb crash]
Lampu cumi! (Nyalakan!)

[Song ends abruptly]
